title: Reading and Normalizing Input
learning_outcomes: Explain what reading and normalizing input contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: missing parameters.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Form values arrive as untrusted strings and may be absent, malformed, or repeated. Normalize them, validate business rules on the server, preserve safe user input when showing errors, and escape values on output. In this lesson, focus on missing parameters; then compare it with empty strings and whitespace. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use reading and normalizing input when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Form values arrive as untrusted strings and may be absent, malformed, or repeated. Normalize them, validate business rules on the server, preserve safe user input when showing errors, and escape values on output. For reading and normalizing input, begin with missing parameters. Also distinguish empty strings and whitespace; scalar versus array input; input normalization. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.
